subject: Occupancy models with very low or high occupancy associated with certain covariates - fix estimates?

messages.author: 1ae392f5bb937067
messages.subject: Occupancy models with very low or high occupancy associated with certain covariates - fix estimates?
parts:
Hello,

I am running occupancy models on birds using habitat type as a nominal covariate. There are 8 habitat types in my dataset, with 7-11 replicates of each habitat type. There were six surveys for each site. For many species, there are either no detections, or naive occupancy = 1, either of which resulting in huge standard errors on my estimates.

Is there a way to set the estimate/psi at something very close to 0 or very close to 1 (depending on whether there are 0 detections or naive occ = 1) so that I can run the models, get realistic estimates, and reasonable answers for model selection? I have been struggling with using the "offset" function, thus far with no success. 

I appreciate any advice! Thank you,

Isabel

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Occupancy models with very low or high occupancy associated with certain covariates - fix estimates?
parts: Hi Isabel, I think your best option here is to go with a BUGS/JAGS model.  This would allow flexibility with boundary estimates, among other things.

messages.author: 254e2a86eb3ba6a4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Occupancy models with very low or high occupancy associated with certain covariates - fix estimates?
parts:
Isabel,

Are you able to assume the detection probability is the same across habitat types even for the species where there are no detections?  And is there enough justification for a particular prior distribution (either uniform or something else) for the detection probability and the probability of presence?  (For whatever it's worth, I think that Dan Linden's suggestion is the way to go.)

Jim
